records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כְּהָכִ֞ין מַלְכ֤וּת רְחַבְעָם֙ וּכְחֶזְקָת֔וֹ עָזַ֖ב אֶת־תּוֹרַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: And it was when was established [the] kingdom of Rehoboam and when [he was] strong, he forsook [the] law of Yahweh, and all Israel with him.
pieces: When Rehoboam's kingdom was firmly established and he had become strong, he abandoned the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all Israel with him.

L.1: And it happened, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and when he was strong, [that] he abandoned the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all Israel with him.

R.1: Rehoboam's kingdom became secure, and he grew strong. Then he turned away from the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all the people of Israel followed him.

decisions.choice: he abandoned the law of Yahweh: strength led to unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: Chronicles often shows a king who becomes secure and then turns from Yahweh (26:16; 32:25). Rehoboam had begun well: for three years he and the people walked in the way of David and Solomon (11:17). Once his kingdom was firm, he left Yahweh's law. The verb "abandon" returns in Yahweh's answer in verse 5.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the people of Rehoboam's kingdom
decisions.reason: Chronicles uses "Israel" for the people of Judah and Benjamin who stayed with Rehoboam, together with those from the north who joined them (11:3, 13-17). They are the true people of Israel in the writer's view, so the name is kept here; verse 6 calls their leaders "the princes of Israel" in the same way.

decisions.choice: when he was strong: when he had grown powerful
decisions.reason: The second phrase is a noun with "his" ("according to his strength"), here meaning the time when his power was firm. It echoes 11:17, where the Levites and others "strengthened" the kingdom of Judah for three years.

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel followed him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the people went the same way as their king, which is what "and all Israel with him" means.

records.heading: Shishak invades Judah

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַֽחֲמִישִׁית֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֔ם עָלָ֛ה שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֥י מָעֲל֖וּ בַּיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was in the year the fifth of King Rehoboam, came up Shishak king of Egypt against Jerusalem, for they had acted unfaithfully against Yahweh,
pieces: In King Rehoboam's fifth year, because they had broken faith with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem,

L.2: And it happened in the fifth year of King Rehoboam [that] Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had acted unfaithfully against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

R.2: So in the fifth year that Rehoboam was king, Shishak, the king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem. This happened because the people had been unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 14:25, with a reason added
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 1 Kings 14:25 almost word for word (Shishak is the pharaoh Sheshonq I; see the note there). Chronicles adds the reason: "because they had acted unfaithfully against Yahweh". Kings only sets the invasion after its list of Judah's sins.

decisions.choice: acted unfaithfully: broke faith with Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb means to break trust, as a wife unfaithful to her husband (Numbers 5:12) or one who takes what belongs to Yahweh (Joshua 7:1). Chronicles uses it for the sin that brings disaster on Israel and Judah (1 Chronicles 10:13; 2 Chronicles 36:14).

decisions.choice: they: the king and the people
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. It looks back to Rehoboam "and all Israel with him" (verse 1).

decisions.choice: the reason placed before the main clause (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the reason first so that the list of Shishak's forces in verse 3 can follow "came up against Jerusalem" directly, as it does in the Hebrew sentence.

decisions.choice: attacked Jerusalem (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 14:25: "came up against" means came to attack. Readable names "the people" as those who were unfaithful (m3).

records.source: בְּאֶ֤לֶף וּמָאתַ֨יִם֙ רֶ֔כֶב וּבְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֗ר לָעָ֞ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֤אוּ עִמּוֹ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לוּבִ֥ים סֻכִּיִּ֖ים וְכוּשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: with thousand and two hundred chariot[s] and with sixty thousand horsemen; and [there was] no number to the people who came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.
pieces: with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen, and troops beyond counting came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.

L.3: with 1,200 chariots and with 60,000 horsemen; and [there was] no number to the people who came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.

R.3: He had 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen. He also brought more soldiers from Egypt than anyone could count. They included Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.

decisions.choice: Libyans and Cushites: peoples serving in the Egyptian army
decisions.reason: The Libyans lived west of Egypt; Shishak's own family was of Libyan descent. The Cushites came from the land south of Egypt along the upper Nile. Both served as soldiers in Egypt's armies. 16:8 mentions them again.

decisions.choice: Sukkiim: a people otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: The name appears only here. It may be a group of desert fighters or scouts serving with the Egyptian army, but this is not certain. The name is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen: the size of Shishak's force
decisions.reason: The numbers are given as "thousand" counts, like the army lists of Numbers (see the note at Numbers 1 on the size of such totals). Kings gives no figures. The point is that Judah could not resist such an army.

decisions.choice: no number to the people: too many to count
decisions.reason: "There was no number" is a common way to say a crowd was countless (Judges 6:5; 7:12). "The people" here means the soldiers.

decisions.choice: the people (Literal); troops (Balanced); soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "people" means an army in the field, worded as elsewhere in the historical books.

records.source: וַיִּלְכֹּ֛ד אֶת־עָרֵ֥י הַמְּצֻר֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And he captured [the] cities of the fortifications which [were] to Judah, and he came as far as Jerusalem.
pieces: He took the fortified cities belonging to Judah and advanced as far as Jerusalem.

L.4: And he captured the fortified cities that [belonged] to Judah, and he came as far as Jerusalem.

R.4: He captured the walled towns of Judah and came all the way to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the fortified cities of Judah: the towns Rehoboam had built up
decisions.reason: Rehoboam had fortified a ring of towns in Judah and stocked them with food, weapons and commanders (11:5-12). They did not stop Shishak. Shishak's own inscription in Egypt lists many towns he attacked in the land.

decisions.choice: walled towns (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for towns strengthened with walls and gates.

records.source: וּֽשְׁמַֽעְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ בָּ֣א אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֔ם וְשָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־נֶאֶסְפ֥וּ אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם מִפְּנֵ֣י שִׁישָׁ֑ק וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַתֶּם֙ עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִ֔י וְאַף־אֲנִ֛י עָזַ֥בְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־שִׁישָֽׁק׃
records.gloss: And Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and [the] princes of Judah who had gathered to Jerusalem from before Shishak, and he said to them, Thus says Yahweh: You have abandoned me, and also I have abandoned you in [the] hand of Shishak.
pieces: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the officials of Judah, who had gathered at Jerusalem for fear of Shishak, and said to them, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: You abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so I have abandoned you to Shishak."

L.5: And Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah, who had gathered to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: You have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so I also have abandoned you into the hand of Shishak."

R.5: The prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah. They had gathered in Jerusalem to escape from Shishak. Shemaiah told them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so now I have abandoned you to Shishak's power."

decisions.choice: Shemaiah the prophet: the prophet of 11:2-4
decisions.reason: Shemaiah had earlier brought Yahweh's word that stopped Rehoboam from going to war against the northern tribes (11:2-4; 1 Kings 12:22-24). Kings does not tell of this second message; Chronicles alone records it.

decisions.choice: you have abandoned me, and I have abandoned you: the sentence matches the sin
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice. Rehoboam abandoned Yahweh's law (verse 1), so Yahweh leaves them to Shishak. Chronicles states this rule elsewhere: "If you abandon him, he will abandon you" (1 Chronicles 28:9; 2 Chronicles 15:2; 24:20). The second half has "also I", stressing that Yahweh answers in kind.

decisions.choice: from before Shishak: in flight from him
decisions.reason: The phrase means "away from the face of" Shishak: the leaders had retreated to Jerusalem to escape his advance (verse 4).

decisions.choice: into the hand of Shishak: into his power
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power or control. Yahweh hands them over to Shishak, as he handed Israel over to enemies in Judges (Judges 2:14; 6:1).

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these court leaders throughout the historical books.

decisions.choice: for fear of Shishak (Balanced); to escape from Shishak (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what "from before Shishak" means (m3).

records.gloss: And humbled themselves [the] princes of Israel and the king, and they said, Righteous [is] Yahweh.
pieces: Then the officials of Israel and the king humbled themselves. "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is righteous," they said.

L.6: And the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves, and they said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] righteous."

R.6: Then the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves. They said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is righteous. He is right to do this."

decisions.choice: humbled themselves: the response Yahweh promised to hear
decisions.reason: At the dedication of the temple Yahweh promised, "if my people ... humble themselves and pray ... I will forgive their sin" (7:14). Here the leaders do the first part of it, and verses 7 and 12 show Yahweh answering. Chronicles uses this verb often for a king's turning back (32:26; 33:12, 19, 23; 34:27).

decisions.choice: Yahweh is righteous: his judgment on us is just
decisions.reason: The words admit that Yahweh is in the right and they are in the wrong. Pharaoh said the same after the plague of hail (Exodus 9:27), and so does Jerusalem in its grief (Lamentations 1:18). It is a confession, not only praise.

decisions.choice: the princes of Israel: the leaders of Judah
decisions.reason: Verse 5 calls them "the princes of Judah". Chronicles uses "Israel" for Rehoboam's people as the true Israel (verse 1).

decisions.choice: He is right to do this (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds a second sentence to show that the words confess that Yahweh's punishment is just (m2).

records.source: וּבִרְא֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ כִּ֣י נִכְנָ֔עוּ הָיָה֩ דְבַר־יְהוָ֨האֶל־שְׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה׀לֵאמֹ֛ר נִכְנְע֖וּ לֹ֣א אַשְׁחִיתֵ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֤ם כִּמְעַט֙ לִפְלֵיטָ֔ה וְלֹא־תִתַּ֧ךְ חֲמָתִ֛י בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּיַד־שִׁישָֽׁק׃
records.gloss: And when saw Yahweh that they had humbled themselves, came [the] word of Yahweh to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; not I will destroy them, and I will give to them like a little for deliverance, and not will pour out my wrath on Jerusalem by [the] hand of Shishak.
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that they had humbled themselves, a word from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves, so I will not destroy them. I will grant them some deliverance, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.

L.7: And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Shemaiah, saying, "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, and I will give them a little deliverance, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will not pour out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw that they had humbled themselves. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Shemaiah this message: "They have humbled themselves, so I will not destroy them. I will rescue them, at least in part. I will not use Shishak to pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a little deliverance: a limited rescue
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "a little" (a partial escape) or "in a little while" (deliverance soon). Verse 8 shows that the rescue is only partial: Jerusalem is spared but the people become Shishak's servants, so the sense "a little" fits best. The word for deliverance often means escape from disaster, or the people who escape it (Ezra 9:8, 13).

decisions.choice: I will not destroy them: Yahweh's answer to their humbling
decisions.reason: Yahweh's words repeat theirs: "they have humbled themselves" twice. His anger is held back because they turned, as he promised at 7:14.

decisions.choice: my wrath will not pour out: Yahweh's anger pictured as a liquid
decisions.reason: Anger that is "poured out" is anger let loose in full (34:21, 25; Jeremiah 7:20). Here it is held back from Jerusalem. "By the hand of Shishak" means through Shishak as Yahweh's instrument.

decisions.choice: some deliverance (Balanced); rescue them, at least in part (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how much deliverance is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: I will not use Shishak (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable states what "by the hand of Shishak" means (m3).

records.source: כִּ֥י יִהְיוּ־ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִ֑ים וְיֵדְעוּ֙ עֲב֣וֹדָתִ֔י וַעֲבוֹדַ֖ת מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: But they will become to him for servants, and they will know my service and [the] service of [the] kingdoms of the lands.
pieces: Yet they will become his servants, so that they may learn what it is to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and what it is to serve the kingdoms of other lands."

L.8: But they will become servants to him, and they will know {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands."

R.8: But they will have to serve him. Then they will learn the difference between serving {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and serving the kingdoms of other lands."

decisions.choice: servants ... my service ... the service of the kingdoms: a wordplay with a lesson
decisions.reason: "Servants" and "service" come from the same Hebrew root. Judah wanted to be free of Yahweh's law (verse 1); now they will serve Shishak and learn by experience how hard serving foreign kings is compared with serving Yahweh. Deuteronomy warned of the same exchange (Deuteronomy 28:47-48).

decisions.choice: become servants to him: become subject to Shishak
decisions.reason: The word for servants here means subjects of a foreign king who must pay tribute, not household slaves. Verse 9 shows what this meant: Shishak carried off the treasures of temple and palace.

decisions.choice: but ... and they will know: a limit, then a purpose
decisions.reason: The first word sets a limit on the rescue promised in verse 7. The second verb tells the purpose of the servitude: so that they will learn.

decisions.choice: servants (every level)
decisions.reason: Literal also has "servants" rather than "slaves", so that the link with "service" stays clear at every level and because the people are subjects, not owned slaves (m2).

decisions.choice: what it is to serve (Balanced); the difference between (Readable); other lands
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what "know my service and the service of the kingdoms" means (m1). "Other" makes clear that the lands are foreign ones.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַל שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַיִם֮ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַם֒ וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־אֹצְר֣וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת־אֹֽצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֶת־הַכֹּ֖ל לָקָ֑ח וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־מָגִנֵּ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And came up Shishak king of Egypt against Jerusalem, and he took [the] treasures of [the] house of Yahweh and [the] treasures of [the] house of the king; the all he took; and he took [the] shields of the gold which made Solomon.
pieces: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem. He carried off the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and those of the king's palace. He took everything, even the gold shields Solomon had made.

L.9: And Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and he took the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the treasures of the house of the king; he took everything. And he took the shields of gold that Solomon had made.

R.9: So Shishak, the king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem. He carried off the treasures from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from the king's palace. He took everything. He even took the gold shields that Solomon had made.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 14:25-26, with two small differences
decisions.reason: Chronicles repeats the opening of 1 Kings 14:25 ("Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem") to return to the story after Shemaiah's message, and then follows 1 Kings 14:26. Kings says "all the shields of gold"; Chronicles has "the shields of gold" without "all". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the shields of gold that Solomon had made: the display shields of 9:15-16
decisions.reason: Solomon made two hundred large shields and three hundred small ones of hammered gold for the House of the Forest of Lebanon (9:15-16; 1 Kings 10:16-17). Now they are gone. The treasure of the temple and the palace is what the servitude of verse 8 costs.

decisions.choice: he took everything: the plunder was complete
decisions.reason: "Everything" stands first for emphasis, as in 1 Kings 14:26.

decisions.choice: the king's palace (Balanced, Readable); the temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 14:26: the same Hebrew word "house" is used for the king's palace and for Yahweh's temple. "So" at the start marks the return to the story of verses 2-4.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ רְחַבְעָם֙ תַּחְתֵּיהֶ֔ם מָגִנֵּ֖י נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְהִפְקִ֗יד עַל־יַד֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרָצִ֔ים הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים פֶּ֖תַח בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And made King Rehoboam in their place shields of bronze, and he entrusted [them] on [the] hand of [the] commanders of the runners, the ones keeping [the] entrance of [the] house of the king.
pieces: King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and entrusted them to the commanders of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the king's palace.

L.10: And King Rehoboam made in their place shields of bronze, and he entrusted [them] to the hand of the commanders of the runners, who kept the entrance of the house of the king.

R.10: So King Rehoboam made shields of bronze to take their place. He put them in the care of the commanders of the guard, the soldiers who guarded the entrance to the king's palace.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 14:27
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1 Kings 14:27; only the spelling of "in their place" differs slightly. Bronze takes the place of gold: the court keeps up the show, but the splendor of Solomon's reign is gone.

decisions.choice: the runners: the king's guard
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 14:27: the "runners" were royal guards who ran before the king's chariot and kept watch at his palace (1 Samuel 22:17; 2 Samuel 15:1).

decisions.choice: the runners (Literal); the guard (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Worded as in 1 Kings 14:27. "Commanders" is kept at every level, as for military leaders elsewhere.

records.source: וַיְהִ֛י מִדֵּי־ב֥וֹא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה בָּ֤אוּ הָרָצִים֙ וּנְשָׂא֔וּם וֶהֱשִׁב֖וּם אֶל־תָּ֥א הָרָצִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was as often as went the king [into the] house of Yahweh, came the runners and carried them, and returned them to [the] guardroom of the runners.
pieces: Whenever the king went into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the guards came and carried the shields, and afterward they brought them back to the guardroom.

L.11: And it happened, as often as the king went into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the runners came and carried them, and they brought them back to the guardroom of the runners.

R.11: Every time the king went to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the guards came and carried the shields in front of him. Then they took them back to the guards' room.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 14:28, with "came" added
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 14:28 says "the runners carried them"; Chronicles says "the runners came and carried them". The sense is the same: the guards came out for the procession.

decisions.choice: carried them and brought them back: the shields were for ceremony
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 14:28: the shields were carried in procession when the king went up to the temple and then stored in the guardroom. They were for display, not for battle.

decisions.choice: the runners (Literal); the guards (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10. Balanced does not repeat "of the guards" after "guardroom".

decisions.choice: in front of him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the shields were carried in procession before the king (m2), as in 1 Kings 14:28.

records.source: וּבְהִכָּֽנְע֗וֹ שָׁ֤ב מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ אַף־יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א לְהַשְׁחִ֖ית לְכָלָ֑ה וְגַם֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה הָיָ֖ה דְּבָרִ֥ים טוֹבִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And when he humbled himself, turned from him [the] anger of Yahweh, and not to destroy to completion; and also in Judah there were things good.
pieces: Because he humbled himself, the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned back from him and did not destroy him completely. And there were also good things in Judah.

L.12: And when he humbled himself, the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned from him, and [it was] not to destroy [him] completely; and also in Judah there were good things.

R.12: Rehoboam humbled himself, so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stopped being angry with him and did not destroy him completely. Also, some good things were still found in Judah.

decisions.choice: when he humbled himself, Yahweh's anger turned: the lesson of the story
decisions.reason: The writer sums up the story: humbling oneself before Yahweh turns his anger away (verses 6-7; 7:14). Judah was punished, but not destroyed.

decisions.choice: good things in Judah: some good was still found there
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that some faithfulness was still found in Judah, which is how the same words are used in 19:3. It may also mean that things went well in Judah after the danger had passed. The first fits the reason given in this verse for sparing the kingdom.

decisions.choice: and not to destroy completely: the anger stopped short of full destruction
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It describes what the turning of Yahweh's anger meant: Judah was not wiped out (compare verse 7).

decisions.choice: did not destroy him completely (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Yahweh's anger, or Yahweh, the subject of "destroy" and supply "him", so the clause reads as a complete sentence (m3).

decisions.choice: were still found (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable expresses the reading chosen in m2 with words from 19:3.

records.source: וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֞ק הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֛ם בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיִּמְלֹ֑ךְ כִּ֣י בֶן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וְאַחַ֣ת שָׁנָה֩ רְחַבְעָ֨ם בְּמָלְכ֜וֹ וּֽשֲׁבַ֨ע עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֣ה׀מָלַ֣ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הָ֠עִיר אֲשֶׁר־בָּחַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָשׂ֨וּם אֶת־שְׁמ֥וֹ שָׁם֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ נַעֲמָ֖ה הָֽעַמֹּנִֽית׃
records.gloss: And strengthened himself King Rehoboam in Jerusalem and reigned; for a son of forty and one year[s was] Rehoboam in his reigning, and seventeen year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem, the city which chose Yahweh to put his name there from all [the] tribes of Israel; and [the] name of his mother [was] Naamah the Ammonite.
pieces: King Rehoboam established himself firmly in Jerusalem and reigned. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had chosen from among all the tribes of Israel as the place for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.

L.13: And King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned. For Rehoboam [was] a son of forty-one years when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name there. And the name of his mother [was] Naamah the Ammonite.

R.13: King Rehoboam made his rule strong in Jerusalem and went on as king. He became king at the age of forty-one, and he ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem. Out of all the tribes of Israel, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had chosen this city as the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be worshiped. Rehoboam's mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.

decisions.choice: the opening formula of 1 Kings 14:21, placed at the end of the reign
decisions.reason: From "Rehoboam was forty-one" on, the verse repeats 1 Kings 14:21 word for word (see the notes there on the formula, the queen mother Naamah and the city Yahweh chose). Chronicles places it near the close of the reign and opens with a new clause: Rehoboam "strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned", that is, his rule recovered after Shishak's attack. The word "for" ties the formula to that clause.

decisions.choice: his mother was Naamah the Ammonite: the queen mother
decisions.reason: Kings and Chronicles name the mothers of the kings of Judah, who held a place of honor at court. Naamah came from Ammon, east of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: a son of forty-one years: forty-one years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: established himself firmly and reigned (Balanced); made his rule strong and went on as king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The rest of the verse keeps the wording of 1 Kings 14:21 at each level. Readable states the meaning of "to put his name there" as the place where Yahweh would be worshiped, as there.

records.heading: The end of Rehoboam's reign

records.source: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ הָרָ֑ע כִּ֣י לֹ֤א הֵכִין֙ לִבּ֔וֹ לִדְר֖וֹשׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And he did the evil, for not he set his heart to seek Yahweh.
pieces: He did what was evil, because he had not set his heart on seeking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: And he did the evil, for he did not set his heart to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: Rehoboam did what was evil. He did not make up his mind to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: he did evil: the verdict of 1 Kings 14:22, changed
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 14:22 says that Judah "did the evil in the eyes of Yahweh" and lists the people's sins. Chronicles names Rehoboam himself, leaves out "in the eyes of Yahweh", and gives the reason in its own words: he did not set his heart to seek Yahweh.

decisions.choice: set his heart to seek Yahweh: the measure of a king in Chronicles
decisions.reason: To "seek" Yahweh in Chronicles is to turn to him in worship, prayer and obedience (1 Chronicles 22:19; 2 Chronicles 7:14; 15:12). "Set the heart" means to fix one's will on it. The verb "set" is the one used in verse 1 for the kingdom being "established": Rehoboam made his kingdom firm but not his heart.

decisions.choice: did what was evil (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say "in the sight of the LORD" here, so the usual verdict wording is shortened. Readable drops "because" and lets the second sentence give the reason.

records.source: וְדִבְרֵ֣י רְחַבְעָ֗ם הָרִאשֹׁנִים֙ וְהָאֲ֣חַרוֹנִ֔ים הֲלֹא־הֵ֨ם כְּתוּבִ֜ים בְּדִבְרֵ֨י שְׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה הַנָּבִ֛יא וְעִדּ֥וֹ הַחֹזֶ֖ה לְהִתְיַחֵ֑שׂ וּמִלְחֲמ֧וֹת רְחַבְעָ֛ם וְיָרָבְעָ֖ם כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And [the] matters of Rehoboam, the first and the last, [are] not they written in [the] words of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer, for enrolling by genealogy? And [the] wars of Rehoboam and Jeroboam [were] all the days.
pieces: The acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, in the genealogical records. There were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.

L.15: And the matters of Rehoboam, the first and the last, are they not written in the words of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, for genealogical enrollment? And [there were] wars of Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days.

R.15: Everything Rehoboam did, from beginning to end, is written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer, in the family records. (A seer was a prophet who received messages from God.) Rehoboam and Jeroboam were always at war with each other.

decisions.choice: the sources named: the words of Shemaiah and Iddo instead of the royal record
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 14:29 points to "the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah". Chronicles points instead to the writings of two prophets, as it does for David and Solomon (1 Chronicles 29:29; 2 Chronicles 9:29). The Hebrew word for "matters" and for "words" is the same, so the line plays on it: the matters of Rehoboam are in the words of the prophets. These writings have not survived.

decisions.choice: for genealogical enrollment: the writings included genealogical records
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and unclear. It may mean the prophets' writings were arranged with genealogical lists, or that Rehoboam's family (11:18-23) was recorded there. Some think the words are out of place in the sentence. The Hebrew is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: the seer: a prophet who sees visions
decisions.reason: "Seer" is an older name for a prophet, one who "sees" what Yahweh shows him (1 Samuel 9:9). Iddo is also named as a source for Solomon (9:29) and Abijah (13:22).

decisions.choice: wars of Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days: as 1 Kings 14:30, in the plural
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 14:30 says "there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days". Chronicles has "wars" and joins the sentence to the source note. It means repeated fighting throughout both reigns, though Rehoboam had been told not to fight to win back the north (11:4).

decisions.choice: are they not written ...?: a question expecting "yes"
decisions.reason: As in Kings, the question means "they are written there" and points the reader to the source.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As for every use of this formula: the question stays at Literal and becomes a statement at Balanced and Readable. "Records" at Balanced and Readable renders the Hebrew "words", meaning their written accounts.

decisions.choice: continually (Balanced); always (Readable)
decisions.reason: "All the days" means all through their reigns.

decisions.choice: (A seer was a prophet who received messages from God.)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "seer" the first time it comes in a chapter (m3).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב רְחַבְעָם֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲבִיָּ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Rehoboam with his fathers and was buried in [the] city of David; and reigned Abijah his son in his place.
pieces: Rehoboam rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David. His son Abijah became king in his place.

L.16: And Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And Abijah his son reigned in his place.

R.16: Rehoboam died and was buried in the City of David. His son Abijah became king after him.

decisions.choice: the close of 1 Kings 14:31, shortened
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 14:31 says Rehoboam was buried "with his fathers" and repeats his mother's name. Chronicles leaves both out. Kings calls his son Abijam; Chronicles calls him Abijah (13:1). It is the same king.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula, as in 9:31: he died and joined his ancestors.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula as worded throughout Kings and Chronicles.
